Scrim.$description: Backdrop behind modals, drawers and bottom sheets — covers the viewport beneath the raised surface. Semi-transparent by design; never use it as a plain background fill.

Hover.$description: The universal hover wash. Lay it OVER the existing surface rather than swapping that surface's colour — this is what lets table rows, list items, menu options, clickable cards and ghost buttons all share one hover treatment on white, tinted or coloured grounds alike.

Pressed.$description: Held-down partner to Overlay/Hover. Same rule: composite it over the existing surface, don't replace the surface.

Selected.$description: Persistent selection wash for rows and items sitting on a ground that is not Background/Page. When the ground is plain, prefer the opaque Background/Selected instead.

Loading.$description: Blanket over content that is refreshing, so a table or card can grey out in place without unmounting. Place the spinner above this layer.

Hover.$description: Hover wash for controls on a dark ground — Background/Inverse toolbars, tooltips, dark headers. Overlay/Hover is invisible there because it darkens rather than lightens.

Pressed.$description: Held-down partner to Overlay/Inverse/Hover, for controls sitting on Background/Inverse.

Page.$description: The application ground — sits behind everything. Deliberately just off white so Background/Raised reads as lifted without depending on shadow alone. Do not use on cards.

Raised.$description: Anything lifted off the page: cards, modals, popovers, menus, sheets. Pair with an elevation shadow and Border/Subtle.

Sunken.$description: Inset regions that should read as pushed into the page — input wells, table headers, code blocks, quiet panels.

Muted.$description: Quiet neutral fill for non-interactive furniture: chip grounds, avatar placeholders, skeleton blocks. Not for controls — use Background/Action/* for anything pressable.

Disabled.$description: Fill for disabled controls (buttons, inputs, selects). Pair with Text/Disabled and Border/Disabled. Shares a value with Background/Muted today; kept as a separate token so the two can diverge.

Inverse.$description: Dark ground for tooltips, toasts and dark headers. The only surface that pairs with Text/Inverse, Icon/Inverse, Border/Inverse and the Overlay/Inverse washes.

Selected.$description: Persistent selection ground for table rows, nav items and chosen menu options. For selected AND hovered, composite Overlay/Hover on top — there is deliberately no third token.

Disabled.$description: Fill of any button whose action is unavailable — every rank that has a face at rest (Primary, Secondary, and their Danger forms). Pair with Border/Action/Disabled, Text/Disabled and Icon/Disabled. Ranks with no face at rest (Tertiary, Tertiary Danger) take Background/Action/Transparent instead and keep no border. Never fade the enabled fill with opacity.

Transparent.$description: Transparent by design — the absence of a fill, not a colour. Used by every rank that has no face at rest (Tertiary, Tertiary Danger) for BOTH its rest state and its disabled state. A ghost control keeps no fill and no border when disabled: it is carried entirely by Text/Disabled and Icon/Disabled. Neutral transparent rather than white-at-zero-alpha, so a hover animating to Overlay/Hover does not interpolate through white.

Default.$description: Fill of the highest-emphasis button — the one action you most want taken. Aim for one per view. Foreground: Text/OnSolid/Default and Icon/OnSolid. Edge: Border/Action/Primary/Default.

Hover.$description: Primary button under the pointer. Never substitute an opacity change — the token carries the intended step.

Default.$description: Fill of the standard secondary button — an opaque white face with Border/Action/Secondary/Default around it. Foreground: Text/OnNeutral. Use when the action is real but not the primary one.

Hover.$description: Aliases Overlay/Hover, so the ghost button darkens whatever is behind it rather than punching an opaque rectangle. This is why ghost buttons survive on panels, toolbars and coloured banners.

Pressed.$description: Aliases Overlay/Pressed. Same compositing rule as Background/Action/Tertiary/Hover — lay it over the existing ground rather than replacing it.

Default.$description: Fill of a destructive primary button: delete, remove, revoke. Reserve for actions that lose data or cannot be undone. Foreground: Text/OnSolid/Default.

Hover.$description: Destructive primary button under the pointer.

Pressed.$description: Destructive primary button while held down.

Default.$description: PENDING RETIREMENT — duplicates Background/Action/Secondary/Default (both gray-00). A secondary-danger button is a neutral white face with Border/Action/Danger/* and Text/Status/Danger/*; it needs no fill of its own.

Hover.$description: PENDING RETIREMENT — duplicates Background/Action/DangerTertiary/Hover. Use that one; the two danger low-emphasis ranks should share a single wash pair.

Pressed.$description: PENDING RETIREMENT — duplicates Background/Action/DangerTertiary/Pressed. Use that one.

Hover.$description: Low-emphasis destructive button under the pointer. Opaque rather than a wash because this variant only ever appears on a light ground.

Pressed.$description: Low-emphasis destructive button while held down.

Default.$description: Box or track fill of an unchecked checkbox, radio or toggle. Pair with Border/Default so the empty control still has an edge.

Disabled.$description: Unchecked control that cannot be changed. Pair with Border/Disabled.

Default.$description: Box or track fill of a checked checkbox, radio or toggle. The tick or knob uses Icon/OnSolid.

Hover.$description: Checked control under the pointer — the compound state that is easy to forget and obvious when missing.

Disabled.$description: Checked but locked. Must stay clearly checked: this is a muted brand-to-grey step, not the unchecked fill.

Subtle.$description: Tinted ground for informational banners, alerts and soft badges. Pair with Text/Status/Info, Icon/Status/Info and Border/Status/Info.

Solid.$description: Filled informational ground for solid badges, toasts, status dots and progress fills. Pair the foreground with Text/OnStatus/Info — never with Text/Status/Info, which is tuned for the Subtle tint.

Subtle.$description: Tinted ground for success banners, alerts and soft badges. Pair with Text/Status/Success, Icon/Status/Success and Border/Status/Success.

Solid.$description: Filled success ground for solid badges, toasts, status dots and progress fills. Pair the foreground with Text/OnStatus/Success — never with Text/Status/Success, which is tuned for the Subtle tint.

Subtle.$description: Tinted ground for warning banners, alerts and soft badges. Pair with Text/Status/Warning, Icon/Status/Warning and Border/Status/Warning.

Solid.$description: Filled warning ground for solid badges, toasts, status dots and progress fills. Pair the foreground with Text/OnStatus/Warning — never with Text/Status/Warning, which is tuned for the Subtle tint.

Subtle.$description: Tinted ground for error/destructive banners, alerts and soft badges. Pair with Text/Status/Danger, Icon/Status/Danger and Border/Status/Danger.

Solid.$description: Filled error/destructive ground for solid badges, toasts, status dots and progress fills. Pair the foreground with Text/OnStatus/Danger — never with Text/Status/Danger, which is tuned for the Subtle tint.

Subtle.$description: Tinted ground for neutral (draft, archived, pending) banners, alerts and soft badges. Pair with Text/Status/Neutral, Icon/Status/Neutral and Border/Status/Neutral.

Solid.$description: Filled neutral (draft, archived, pending) ground for solid badges, toasts, status dots and progress fills. Pair the foreground with Text/OnStatus/Neutral — never with Text/Status/Neutral, which is tuned for the Subtle tint.

Strong.$description: Highest-contrast text: headings, key figures, the one phrase that must land first. Not for body copy — over-using it flattens the hierarchy.

Regular.$description: Default body copy, form labels and values. The token you reach for unless you have a reason not to.

Subtle.$description: De-emphasised text: captions, helper text, timestamps, secondary metadata. Still passes contrast on Background/Page — it is quiet, not disabled.

Placeholder.$description: The prompt shown inside an empty input. Kept separate from Text/Disabled so an empty field never reads as a locked one, even though they share a value today.

Disabled.$description: Text in a control that cannot be used. Pair with Background/Disabled and Border/Disabled. Never use it merely to de-emphasise — that is Text/Subtle.

Inverse.$description: Text on a dark ground. Only valid on Background/Inverse (tooltips, toasts, dark headers).

OnNeutral.$description: Label on the white secondary button (Background/Action/Secondary). Deliberately darker than the board's original grey, which read as disabled on a white face.

Default.$description: Label on a filled action — Background/Action/Primary and Background/Action/Danger. Do not use on Background/Action/Secondary, which is light; that is Text/OnNeutral.

Disabled.$description: PENDING RETIREMENT — no consumer. A disabled button is not a solid fill any more, it is Background/Action/Disabled, so its label is Text/Disabled. Kept only until the last reference is confirmed gone.

Default.$description: Brand-coloured interactive text: ghost button labels, links, inline actions. Signals 'this is clickable' without a fill.

Hover.$description: Interactive text under the pointer. Applies to links and ghost labels alike.

Info.$description: Informational text on Background/Status/Info/Subtle — banner copy, badge labels, helper notes.

Neutral.$description: Neutral status text on Background/Status/Neutral/Subtle — draft, archived, pending.

Default.$description: Error text: form validation messages, destructive confirmations, danger badge labels on Background/Status/Danger/Subtle. This is the single error-text token — there is no rival value.

Pressed.$description: Error text while an interactive error element is held down. A state of Text/Status/Danger/Default, not an alternative to it.

Info.$description: Label on the filled Background/Status/Info/Solid ground — solid badges, toasts.

Success.$description: Label on the filled Background/Status/Success/Solid ground.

Warning.$description: Label on the filled Background/Status/Warning/Solid ground. Dark, not white — warning's solid fill is a light yellow, and white on it fails contrast. This is the one family that breaks the pattern.

Danger.$description: Label on the filled Background/Status/Danger/Solid ground.

Neutral.$description: Label on the filled Background/Status/Neutral/Solid ground.

Strong.$description: Highest-contrast glyph, matching Text/Strong. For icons that carry the same weight as a heading.

Regular.$description: Default glyph colour, matching Text/Regular. Use for icons sitting alongside body copy.

Subtle.$description: De-emphasised glyph: chevrons, affordance hints, decorative marks. Matches Text/Subtle.

Disabled.$description: Glyph in a control that cannot be used. Matches Text/Disabled.

Inverse.$description: Glyph on a dark ground. Only valid on Background/Inverse.

OnSolid.$description: Glyph on a filled action — Background/Action/Primary, Background/Action/Danger — and the tick or knob inside Background/Action/Control/Checked.

Action.$description: Brand-coloured interactive glyph: icon buttons, inline action affordances. Matches Text/Action/Default so an icon and its label agree.

Placeholder.$description: The deliberate 'you have not swapped this yet' colour for an unfilled icon slot. It is the ONE glyph token that must never take its colour from context: everything else binds Icon/Current so it adapts, and the placeholder stays loud precisely so an unswapped slot is impossible to miss. Never use it on a real icon.

Info.$description: Informational glyph — the (i) in a banner, a status dot. Sits MORE saturated than Text/Status/Info on purpose: a glyph carries less visual mass than a run of text, so matching the text value would wash it out.

Success.$description: Success glyph — tick, filled dot. More saturated than Text/Status/Success, which is near-black and would read as a neutral tick.

Warning.$description: Warning glyph — triangle, exclamation. More saturated than Text/Status/Warning, which reads brown at glyph scale and loses the yellow identity.

Danger.$description: Error glyph — alert circle, cross. Matches Text/Status/Danger/Default; red needs no correction at glyph scale.

Neutral.$description: Neutral status glyph — the dot on a draft, archived or pending badge.

Divider.$description: Rules and separators only — between list rows, menu sections, toolbar groups. Split from Border/Disabled so divider weight can be tuned without moving every disabled control edge.

Subtle.$description: Quiet container edges: cards, panels, popovers. Pairs with Background/Raised.

Default.$description: Standard control edge at rest. If you are drawing an input specifically, prefer Border/Field/Default — it carries the full state set.

Strong.$description: Emphasised edge for a control that needs to assert itself, and the hovered step of Border/Default.

Disabled.$description: Edge of a control that cannot be used. Pair with Background/Disabled and Text/Disabled.

Inverse.$description: Edge on a dark ground. Only valid on Background/Inverse.

Selected.$description: Edge marking a persistent selection: active tab underline, selected card, chosen option. Pair with Background/Selected on the ground.

Disabled.$description: Edge of any disabled button that has a face. It does real work: Background/Action/Disabled alone is 1.15:1 against a white page, so without this edge the control disappears. Ghost ranks deliberately get no disabled edge.

Default.$description: Edge of a primary button. Tracks Background/Action/Primary/Default exactly, so a filled button's edge is invisible and an outlined one reads as the same rank.

Hover.$description: Primary button edge under the pointer. Tracks Background/Action/Primary/Hover.

Pressed.$description: Primary button edge while held down. Tracks Background/Action/Primary/Pressed.

Default.$description: Edge of the secondary button — the line that makes Background/Action/Secondary read as a button at all, since its fill is white.

Hover.$description: Secondary button edge under the pointer.

Pressed.$description: Secondary button edge while held down. Shares Hover's value deliberately; the fill carries the pressed signal.

Default.$description: Edge of a destructive button. Tracks Background/Action/Danger/Default, and is the outline that gives Background/Action/DangerTertiary its shape.

Hover.$description: Destructive button edge under the pointer.

Pressed.$description: Destructive button edge while held down.

Default.$description: Input, textarea and select edge at rest. Use this rather than Border/Default on form controls: it is the entry point to the full field state set (Hover, Error, Disabled, plus Focus).

Hover.$description: Field edge under the pointer, before focus.

Error.$description: Field edge in a validation error state. Deliberately the full-strength red, not the pale status outline — a 1px edge needs the weight. Pair with Text/Status/Danger/Default on the message below.

Disabled.$description: Field edge when the input cannot be used. Pair with Background/Disabled and Text/Disabled.

Info.$description: Outline around an informational banner or soft badge, paired with Background/Status/Info/Subtle.

Success.$description: Outline around a success banner or soft badge, paired with Background/Status/Success/Subtle.

Warning.$description: Outline around a warning banner or soft badge, paired with Background/Status/Warning/Subtle.

Danger.$description: Outline around an error banner or soft badge, paired with Background/Status/Danger/Subtle. NOT for input error edges — that is Border/Field/Error, which is stronger.

Neutral.$description: Outline around a neutral banner or soft badge, paired with Background/Status/Neutral/Subtle.

Ring.$description: Keyboard focus ring, 2px, drawn OUTSIDE the control so focusing never shifts layout. Required on every focusable element. It stacks with other edges — a focused invalid field shows both this and Border/Field/Error.

Inner.$description: 1px light ring drawn between the control and Border/Focus/Ring. Needed so focus stays visible on dark and saturated fills, where the ring alone can blend into the button.

Dark.$description: Fixed logo mark colour. Not a semantic token — it describes one asset, not a role, and is a candidate to move out of this collection to the Logo page.

Purple.$description: Fixed logo mark colour. Not a semantic token — see Brand/Logo/Dark.

Green.$description: Fixed logo mark colour. Not a semantic token — see Brand/Logo/Dark.
